You are comparing two drafts written from the same brief. Read no other file, and do not run commands or browse; judge only the text below.

Brief: Write the README's opening paragraph and its Install and update section for the `tidy-hooks` plugin.

<<<DRAFT A
`tidy-hooks` is a Claude and Codex plugin that blocks `git commit` when staged files contain merge markers. If Node.js is missing, the hook fails open and commits proceed.

## Install and update

### Claude

Install:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add example/tidy
claude plugin install tidy-hooks@tidy
```

Update:

```sh
claude plugin update tidy-hooks@tidy
```

### Codex

Install:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add example/tidy
codex plugin add tidy-hooks@tidy
```

Codex skips plugin hooks until you review and trust them.

Update:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace upgrade tidy
```

Then restart Codex.
DRAFT A>>>

`tidy-hooks` is a Claude and Codex plugin that blocks `git commit` when staged files contain merge markers. If Node.js is missing, commits proceed.


To update:

```sh
claude plugin update tidy-hooks@tidy
```

### Codex

Install the plugin:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add example/tidy
codex plugin add tidy-hooks@tidy
```

To update, run this command, then restart Codex:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace upgrade tidy
```

items.title: Thinking
items.text:
I'm weighing the two drafts: A's wording is a bit redundant but clearer, and A puts the trust note after install, which makes sense since hooks stay skipped until trusted. B reads better in sequence, with the restart coming before the update command, though neither says how to actually grant trust. A's closing "Then restart Codex." comes after the command.

I'm comparing the two drafts' labels and sequencing: A uses matching "Install:" and "Update:" headings, while B mixes "Install the plugin:" with "To update:". B's trust warning before install is a good choice for a reader, and A's "fails open" is jargon but makes the behavior clear. On balance I think A has a slight edge for readability, though the reader experience is close to even.

A labels Install and Update the same way in both sections, puts the Codex trust note right after the install step it affects, and says the hook fails open, while B mixes 'Install the plugin:' with 'To update:'."}
